questions.q: What gap do Sharing Rules fill, per this lesson?
options: Visibility needs that ownership and the Role Hierarchy alone don't cover, without restructuring the hierarchy itself
They replace the need for licenses entirely
They control which fields are visible, not which records
They determine which Profile a user is assigned
questions.explain: Sharing Rules extend record visibility beyond the ownership + Role Hierarchy default, without hierarchy changes.

questions.q: What does an ownership-based sharing rule use as its criterion for sharing a record?
options: Who owns the record
The record's field values, regardless of owner
The record's creation date only
The user's license type
questions.explain: Ownership-based rules share based on who owns the record, e.g. everyone in a given role.

questions.q: What does a criteria-based sharing rule use as its criterion for sharing a record?
options: Field values on the record itself, regardless of who owns it
Exclusively who owns the record, same as ownership-based rules
The user's Permission Set assignments
The record's related list contents only
questions.explain: Criteria-based rules key off field values on the record, e.g. Stage = Closed Won and Amount > $100,000.

questions.q: For 'share every Opportunity worth over $100,000 with the Executive team, regardless of owner,' which sharing rule type fits, per this lesson's example?
options: A criteria-based sharing rule, since it depends on the Amount field value, not who owns the record
An ownership-based sharing rule, since it's about a team seeing records
Neither type can accomplish this in Salesforce
A Role Hierarchy change, not a sharing rule at all
questions.explain: Because it targets records based on a field (Amount), not ownership, this is exactly a criteria-based rule's use case.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say an analyst should recognize Sharing Rules as a concept?
options: So a report including records a user doesn't own and isn't above in the hierarchy isn't mistaken for a data leak or misconfiguration
Because Sharing Rules eliminate the need to understand the Role Hierarchy at all
Because Sharing Rules are only relevant to Salesforce administrators, never analysts
Because Sharing Rules replace the need for Profiles
questions.explain: The lesson frames recognizing sharing rules as the correct explanation for legitimate, working visibility extensions.
